subject.title: Feature: Add per-model generation timeout config

question: Should OpenClaw expose a supported per-model attempt timeout through the existing request-timeout path, or introduce a distinct total-generation timeout with different semantics?
rationale: The issue and comments describe multiple materially different failure modes—hung transport calls, continuously streaming reasoning, and first-token delay—so a public setting cannot be selected safely without defining what it measures and how fallback consumes it.

options.title: Adopt one per-model request timeout
options.body: Expose and document a single per-model request/attempt timeout, preserve the existing global run timeout, and make first-token and repetition controls separate work.

options.title: Add a distinct generation budget
options.body: Introduce a new non-resetting total-generation budget only if maintainers need semantics that the existing request-timeout path cannot represent.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Land only narrowly scoped cloud-thinking timeout fixes until a broader timeout policy and migration story are agreed.

recommendation.title: Adopt one per-model request timeout
recommendation.body: Expose and document a single per-model request/attempt timeout, preserve the existing global run timeout, and make first-token and repetition controls separate work.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior maintainer review already separated the timeout modes and mapped the decision surface across config, runner, and fallback behavior.
